title: Pogue's Run Trail History
lead: How a long-running community effort connected neighborhoods by trail and waterway.
paragraphs: The Pogue's Run Trail was first envisioned in the 1994 Greenways Master Plan as a way to connect neighborhoods and improve access to parks and waterways on Indianapolis's near eastside.
Initial segments opened over several years, but major gaps remained. Community advocates kept the project moving through planning meetings, funding rounds, and hands-on stewardship projects.

Bridge and infrastructure work near Nowland Avenue became a key milestone before final trail funding could move ahead. After years of effort by local partners and volunteers, construction accelerated and major connections were completed.
The current route now links critical neighborhood destinations and opens new opportunities for recreation, habitat restoration, and community programming.
